4//! Fine rasterization stage of the rendering pipeline.
5//!
6//! This module implements the fine rasterization phase, which processes tiles at the pixel level.
7//! It supports both high-precision (f32) and low-precision (u8) rendering paths, along with
8//! various paint types including solid colors, gradients, images, and blurred rounded rectangles.

45/// Offset to shift from pixel corner to pixel center for sampling.
46const PIXEL_CENTER_OFFSET: f64 = 0.5;
47
48/// Number of color components per pixel (RGBA).
49pub(crate) const COLOR_COMPONENTS: usize = 4;
50
51/// Number of color components in a single column of a tile (height * components).
52pub(crate) const TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS: usize = Tile::HEIGHT as usize * COLOR_COMPONENTS;
53
54/// Size of the scratch buffer used for intermediate rendering operations.
55/// Sized to hold a full wide tile with all color components.
56pub const SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE: usize = WideTile::WIDTH as usize * Tile::HEIGHT as usize * COLOR_COMPONENTS;
57
58/// Type alias for a scratch buffer that can hold a full wide tile's worth of data.
59pub type ScratchBuf<F> = [F; SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE];

61/// Trait for numeric types used in fine rasterization.
62///
63/// This trait abstracts over `f32` and `u8` to allow the same rendering logic
64/// to work with both high-precision (floating-point) and low-precision (integer)
65/// representations. This enables performance optimizations while maintaining accuracy
66/// where needed.
67pub trait Numeric: Copy + Default + Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Send + Sync + 'static {
68    /// The zero value for this numeric type (0.0 for f32, 0 for u8).
69    const ZERO: Self;
70
71    /// The maximum opacity value for this numeric type (1.0 for f32, 255 for u8).
72    const ONE: Self;
73}
74
75impl Numeric for f32 {
76    const ZERO: Self = 0.0;
77    const ONE: Self = 1.0;
78}
79
80impl Numeric for u8 {
81    const ZERO: Self = 0;
82    const ONE: Self = 255;
83}
84
85/// Trait for SIMD vector types that can convert between f32 and u8 representations.
86///
87/// This trait enables efficient batch conversions between different numeric representations
88/// during rendering operations, supporting both high-precision and low-precision rendering paths.
89pub trait NumericVec<S: Simd>: Copy + Clone + Send + Sync {
90    /// Convert from a SIMD vector of f32 values to this type.
91    fn from_f32(simd: S, val: f32x16<S>) -> Self;
92
93    /// Convert from a SIMD vector of u8 values to this type.
94    fn from_u8(simd: S, val: u8x16<S>) -> Self;
95}
96
97impl<S: Simd> NumericVec<S> for f32x16<S> {
98    #[inline(always)]
99    fn from_f32(_: S, val: Self) -> Self {
100        val
101    }
102
103    #[inline(always)]
104    fn from_u8(simd: S, val: u8x16<S>) -> Self {
105        let converted = u8_to_f32(val);
106        converted * Self::splat(simd, 1.0 / 255.0)
107    }
108}
109
110impl<S: Simd> NumericVec<S> for u8x16<S> {
111    #[inline(always)]
112    fn from_f32(simd: S, val: f32x16<S>) -> Self {
113        let v1 = f32x16::splat(simd, 255.0);
114        let v2 = f32x16::splat(simd, 0.5);
115        let mulled = val.mul_add(v1, v2);
116
117        f32_to_u8(mulled)
118    }
119
120    #[inline(always)]
121    fn from_u8(_: S, val: Self) -> Self {
122        val
123    }
124}
125
126/// Convert a SIMD vector of u8 values to f32 values.
127///
128/// This function efficiently converts 16 u8 values to their f32 equivalents using SIMD operations,
129/// preserving the values without normalization (i.e., 255 becomes 255.0, not 1.0).
130#[inline(always)]
131pub(crate) fn u8_to_f32<S: Simd>(val: u8x16<S>) -> f32x16<S> {
132    let simd = val.simd;
133    let zeroes = u8x16::splat(simd, 0);
134
135    let zip1 = simd.zip_high_u8x16(val, zeroes);
136    let zip2 = simd.zip_low_u8x16(val, zeroes);
137
138    let p1 = simd.zip_low_u8x16(zip2, zeroes).bitcast::<u32x4<S>>().to_float::<f32x4<S>>();
139    let p2 = simd.zip_high_u8x16(zip2, zeroes).bitcast::<u32x4<S>>().to_float::<f32x4<S>>();
140    let p3 = simd.zip_low_u8x16(zip1, zeroes).bitcast::<u32x4<S>>().to_float::<f32x4<S>>();
141    let p4 = simd.zip_high_u8x16(zip1, zeroes).bitcast::<u32x4<S>>().to_float::<f32x4<S>>();
142
143    simd.combine_f32x8(simd.combine_f32x4(p1, p2), simd.combine_f32x4(p3, p4))
144}

146/// Trait for SIMD vector types used in compositing and blending operations.
147///
148/// This trait abstracts over different SIMD vector widths (f32x16 for high-precision,
149/// u8x32 for low-precision) to enable efficient batch processing of pixel data during
150/// blending and compositing.
151pub trait CompositeType<N: Numeric, S: Simd>: Copy + Clone + Send + Sync {
152    /// The number of numeric values this composite type can hold.
153    const LENGTH: usize;
154
155    /// Load values from a slice into this composite type.
156    fn from_slice(simd: S, slice: &[N]) -> Self;
157
158    /// Create a composite type by repeating a single RGBA color across all elements.
159    fn from_color(simd: S, color: [N; 4]) -> Self;
160}
161
162impl<S: Simd> CompositeType<f32, S> for f32x16<S> {
163    const LENGTH: usize = 16;
164
165    #[inline(always)]
166    fn from_slice(simd: S, slice: &[f32]) -> Self {
167        <Self as SimdBase<_>>::from_slice(simd, slice)
168    }
169
170    #[inline(always)]
171    fn from_color(simd: S, color: [f32; 4]) -> Self {
172        Self::block_splat(f32x4::from_slice(simd, &color[..]))
173    }
174}
175
176impl<S: Simd> CompositeType<u8, S> for u8x32<S> {
177    const LENGTH: usize = 32;
178
179    #[inline(always)]
180    fn from_slice(simd: S, slice: &[u8]) -> Self {
181        <Self as SimdBase<_>>::from_slice(simd, slice)
182    }
183
184    #[inline(always)]
185    fn from_color(simd: S, color: [u8; 4]) -> Self {
186        u32x8::block_splat(u32x4::splat(simd, u32::from_ne_bytes(color))).to_bytes()
187    }
188}

190/// A kernel for performing fine rasterization.
191///
192/// This trait defines the interface for tile-level rendering operations, abstracting over
193/// different numeric precisions (f32 vs u8). Implementations provide the low-level pixel
194/// manipulation, blending, and painting operations needed to render tiles.
195///
196/// The two main implementations are:
197/// - [`F32Kernel`]: High-precision rendering using 32-bit floating-point values
198/// - [`U8Kernel`]: Low-precision rendering using 8-bit integer values
199pub trait FineKernel<S: Simd>: Send + Sync + 'static {
200    /// The basic underlying numerical type of the kernel (f32 or u8).
201    type Numeric: Numeric;
202
203    /// The SIMD composite type used for efficient batch blending and compositing operations.
204    type Composite: CompositeType<Self::Numeric, S>;
205
206    /// The SIMD vector type used for conversions between u8 and f32 representations.
207    type NumericVec: NumericVec<S>;
208
209    /// Extract and convert a premultiplied color to the kernel's numeric type.
210    ///
211    /// Converts RGBA components from the standard premultiplied color format to
212    /// the kernel's internal representation (e.g., 0.0-1.0 for f32, 0-255 for u8).
213    fn extract_color(color: PremulColor) -> [Self::Numeric; 4];
214
215    /// Pack the blend buffer contents into the output region.
216    ///
217    /// Converts from the internal scratch buffer format to the output tile format,
218    /// writing the results to the provided region.
219    fn pack(simd: S, region: &mut Region<'_>, blend_buf: &[Self::Numeric]);
220
221    /// Unpack the region contents back into the blend buffer.
222    ///
223    /// Performs the reverse of `pack`, reading pixel data from the tile region
224    /// and loading it into the scratch buffer for further processing.
225    fn unpack(simd: S, region: &mut Region<'_>, blend_buf: &mut [Self::Numeric]);
226
227    /// Apply a filter to a layer.
228    ///
229    /// This is used for applying filters to whole layers, which is necessary for
230    /// spatial filters (like blur) that need to access neighboring pixels. The filter
231    /// is applied in-place to the provided pixmap.
232    ///
233    /// The transform parameter is used to scale filter parameters based on the current
234    /// transformation matrix (e.g., zoom level), ensuring filters look consistent
235    /// regardless of scale.
236    fn filter_layer(pixmap: &mut Pixmap, filter: &Filter, layer_manager: &mut LayerManager, transform: Affine);
237
238    /// Fill the target buffer with a solid color.
239    ///
240    /// Efficiently replicates the given RGBA color across all pixels in the target buffer.
241    fn copy_solid(simd: S, target: &mut [Self::Numeric], color: [Self::Numeric; 4]);
242    /// Create a painter for rendering gradients.
243    ///
244    /// Returns a painter that can render linear, radial, or sweep gradients based on
245    /// pre-computed t values (gradient interpolation parameters).
246    fn gradient_painter<'a>(simd: S, gradient: &'a EncodedGradient, t_vals: &'a [f32]) -> impl Painter + 'a {
247        simd.vectorize(
248            #[inline(always)]
249            || GradientPainter::new(simd, gradient, t_vals),
250        )
251    }
252
253    /// Create a painter for rendering gradients with undefined region support.
254    ///
255    /// Similar to `gradient_painter`, but with support for masking undefined locations
256    /// (used for radial gradients that may have mathematically undefined regions).
257    ///
258    /// This is intentionally a duplicate of the default [`FineKernel::gradient_painter`]
259    /// implementation--the `U8Kernel` overrides that method, but not this one.
260    fn gradient_painter_with_undefined<'a>(simd: S, gradient: &'a EncodedGradient, t_vals: &'a [f32]) -> impl Painter + 'a {
261        simd.vectorize(
262            #[inline(always)]
263            || GradientPainter::new(simd, gradient, t_vals),
264        )
265    }
266    /// Create a painter for rendering axis-aligned nearest-neighbor images.
267    ///
268    /// Optimized painter for images with `Low` quality and no skewing component in their
269    /// transform. This is the fastest image rendering path.
270    fn plain_nn_image_painter<'a>(simd: S, image: &'a EncodedImage, pixmap: &'a Pixmap, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter + 'a {
271        simd.vectorize(
272            #[inline(always)]
273            || PlainNNImagePainter::new(simd, image, pixmap, start_x, start_y),
274        )
275    }
276
277    /// Create a painter for rendering nearest-neighbor images with transforms.
278    ///
279    /// Similar to `plain_nn_image_painter`, but supports arbitrary affine transforms
280    /// including skewing and rotation.
281    fn nn_image_painter<'a>(simd: S, image: &'a EncodedImage, pixmap: &'a Pixmap, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter + 'a {
282        simd.vectorize(
283            #[inline(always)]
284            || NNImagePainter::new(simd, image, pixmap, start_x, start_y),
285        )
286    }
287
288    /// Create a painter for rendering images with `Medium` quality filtering.
289    ///
290    /// Uses bilinear filtering for smoother appearance than nearest-neighbor.
291    fn medium_quality_image_painter<'a>(simd: S, image: &'a EncodedImage, pixmap: &'a Pixmap, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter + 'a {
292        simd.vectorize(
293            #[inline(always)]
294            || FilteredImagePainter::<S, 1>::new(simd, image, pixmap, start_x, start_y),
295        )
296    }
297
298    /// Create a painter for rendering axis-aligned images with `Medium` quality filtering.
299    ///
300    /// Optimized painter for images with bilinear filtering and no skewing component.
301    fn plain_medium_quality_image_painter<'a>(simd: S, image: &'a EncodedImage, pixmap: &'a Pixmap, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter + 'a {
302        simd.vectorize(
303            #[inline(always)]
304            || FilteredImagePainter::<S, 1>::new(simd, image, pixmap, start_x, start_y),
305        )
306    }
307
308    /// Create a painter for rendering images with `High` quality filtering.
309    ///
310    /// Uses high-quality filtering for the best visual appearance.
311    fn high_quality_image_painter<'a>(simd: S, image: &'a EncodedImage, pixmap: &'a Pixmap, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter + 'a {
312        simd.vectorize(
313            #[inline(always)]
314            || FilteredImagePainter::<S, 2>::new(simd, image, pixmap, start_x, start_y),
315        )
316    }
317
318    /// Create a painter for rendering blurred rounded rectangles.
319    ///
320    /// Efficiently renders rounded rectangles with gaussian blur applied,
321    /// computing the blur analytically rather than as a post-process.
322    fn blurred_rounded_rectangle_painter(simd: S, rect: &EncodedBlurredRoundedRectangle, start_x: f64, start_y: f64) -> impl Painter {
323        simd.vectorize(
324            #[inline(always)]
325            || BlurredRoundedRectFiller::new(simd, rect, start_x, start_y),
326        )
327    }
328    /// Apply a mask to the destination buffer.
329    ///
330    /// Multiplies each pixel in the destination by the corresponding mask value,
331    /// effectively masking out or reducing the opacity of pixels.
332    fn apply_mask(simd: S, dest: &mut [Self::Numeric], src: impl Iterator<Item = Self::NumericVec>);
333
334    /// Apply a painter to render content into the destination buffer.
335    ///
336    /// Invokes the painter to generate pixel values and writes them to the destination.
337    fn apply_painter<'a>(simd: S, dest: &mut [Self::Numeric], painter: impl Painter + 'a);
338
339    /// Apply an image tint to an already-painted buffer.
340    ///
341    /// This is called as a post-pass after `apply_painter`, only when a tint is
342    /// present. Keeping tint application out of the per-pixel iterator avoids
343    /// regressing the non-tinted fast path.
344    fn apply_tint(simd: S, dest: &mut [Self::Numeric], tint: &Tint);
345
346    /// Perform alpha compositing with a solid color over the target buffer.
347    ///
348    /// Blends a solid RGBA color over the existing contents using standard alpha compositing
349    /// (Porter-Duff source-over). Optionally applies additional per-pixel alpha values.
350    fn alpha_composite_solid(simd: S, target: &mut [Self::Numeric], src: [Self::Numeric; 4], alphas: Option<&[u8]>);
351
352    /// Perform alpha compositing with a source buffer over the destination buffer.
353    ///
354    /// Blends the source buffer contents over the destination using standard alpha compositing.
355    /// Optionally applies additional per-pixel alpha values.
356    fn alpha_composite_buffer(simd: S, dest: &mut [Self::Numeric], src: &[Self::Numeric], alphas: Option<&[u8]>);
357
358    /// Blend the source into the destination with a specified blend mode.
359    ///
360    /// Applies advanced blending operations (e.g., multiply, screen, overlay) as specified
361    /// by the blend mode. Optionally applies additional per-pixel alpha values.
362    fn blend(
363        simd: S,
364        dest: &mut [Self::Numeric],
365        start_x: u16,
366        start_y: u16,
367        src: impl Iterator<Item = Self::Composite>,
368        blend_mode: BlendMode,
369        alphas: Option<&[u8]>,
370        mask: Option<&Mask>,
371    );
372}

374/// Fine rasterizer for processing tiles at the pixel level.
375///
376/// This structure maintains the state and scratch buffers needed for tile-based rendering.
377/// It processes rendering commands and manages a stack of blend buffers for layer composition.
378#[derive(Debug)]
379pub struct Fine<S: Simd, T: FineKernel<S>> {
380    /// The (x, y) coordinates of the currently active wide tile being rendered.
381    pub(crate) wide_coords: (u16, u16),
382
383    /// Stack of blend buffers for managing layers and composition.
384    ///
385    /// Each layer pushes a new buffer onto this stack, and layers are composited
386    /// by popping and blending with the buffer below.
387    pub(crate) blend_buf: Vec<ScratchBuf<T::Numeric>>,
388
389    /// Intermediate buffer used by painters to store generated pixel data before compositing.
390    pub(crate) paint_buf: ScratchBuf<T::Numeric>,
391
392    /// Buffer for storing gradient interpolation parameters (t values).
393    ///
394    /// Gradients pre-compute these values for efficiency before color lookup.
395    pub(crate) f32_buf: Vec<f32>,
396
397    /// The SIMD context used for vectorized operations.
398    pub(crate) simd: S,
399}
400
401impl<S: Simd, T: FineKernel<S>> Fine<S, T> {
402    /// Create a new fine rasterizer with the given SIMD context.
403    ///
404    /// Initializes all scratch buffers and sets up the initial blend buffer.
405    pub fn new(simd: S) -> Self {
406        Self {
407            simd,
408            wide_coords: (0, 0),
409            blend_buf: vec![[T::Numeric::ZERO; SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE]],
410            f32_buf: vec![0.0; SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE / 4],
411            paint_buf: [T::Numeric::ZERO; SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE],
412        }
413    }
414
415    /// Set the coordinates of the wide tile currently being rendered.
416    ///
417    /// This is used by painters and other operations to compute absolute pixel positions.
418    pub fn set_coords(&mut self, x: u16, y: u16) {
419        self.wide_coords = (x, y);
420    }
421
422    /// Clear the current blend buffer to a solid color.
423    ///
424    /// This efficiently fills the entire buffer with the given premultiplied color.
425    pub fn clear(&mut self, premul_color: PremulColor) {
426        let converted_color = T::extract_color(premul_color);
427        let blend_buf = self.blend_buf.last_mut().unwrap();
428
429        T::copy_solid(self.simd, blend_buf, converted_color);
430    }
431
432    /// Writes the current blend buffer contents to the output region.
433    ///
434    /// This copies pixel data from the internal scratch buffer to the tile region,
435    /// converting the layout from the internal representation to the output format.
436    pub fn pack(&self, region: &mut Region<'_>) {
437        let blend_buf = self.blend_buf.last().unwrap();
438
439        T::pack(self.simd, region, blend_buf);
440    }
441
442    /// Reads the region contents back into the blend buffer.
443    ///
444    /// This copies pixel data from the tile region to the internal scratch buffer,
445    /// performing the reverse operation of `pack`. This is typically used when a layer
446    /// needs to be read back for further processing.
447    pub fn unpack(&mut self, region: &mut Region<'_>) {
448        let blend_buf = self.blend_buf.last_mut().unwrap();
449
450        T::unpack(self.simd, region, blend_buf);
451    }
452
453    /// Apply a filter to a layer.
454    ///
455    /// This applies the filter using the kernel's implementation, mutating the layer.
456    pub fn filter_layer(&self, pixmap: &mut Pixmap, filter: &Filter, layer_manager: &mut LayerManager, transform: Affine) {
457        T::filter_layer(pixmap, filter, layer_manager, transform);
458    }
459
460    /// Execute a rendering command on the current tile.
461    ///
462    /// This is the main dispatch method that processes different command types including
463    /// fills, clips, blends, filters, masks, and buffer operations.
464    pub(crate) fn run_cmd(&mut self, cmd: &Cmd, alphas: &[u8], paints: &[EncodedPaint], image_resolver: &dyn ImageResolver, attrs: &CommandAttrs) {
465        match cmd {
466            Cmd::Fill(f) => {
467                let fill_attrs = &attrs.fill[f.attrs_idx as usize];
468                self.fill(
469                    usize::from(f.x),
470                    usize::from(f.width),
471                    &fill_attrs.paint,
472                    fill_attrs.blend_mode,
473                    paints,
474                    image_resolver,
475                    None,
476                    fill_attrs.mask.as_ref(),
477                );
478            }
479            Cmd::AlphaFill(s) => {
480                let fill_attrs = &attrs.fill[s.attrs_idx as usize];
481                let alpha_idx = fill_attrs.alpha_idx(s.alpha_offset) as usize;
482                self.fill(
483                    usize::from(s.x),
484                    usize::from(s.width),
485                    &fill_attrs.paint,
486                    fill_attrs.blend_mode,
487                    paints,
488                    image_resolver,
489                    Some(&alphas[alpha_idx..]),
490                    fill_attrs.mask.as_ref(),
491                );
492            }
493            Cmd::Filter(_filter, _) => {
494                // TODO: Apply non-spatial filters here; spatial filters need layer-level processing
495                //
496                // Spatial filters (e.g., Gaussian blur) need neighboring pixels and must be
497                // rendered to a pixmap for layer-level processing. Non-spatial effects (e.g.,
498                // color matrix, component transfer) can be processed here directly on the
499                // blend buffer per-pixel as wide commands.
500            }
501            Cmd::PushBuf(_layer_kind, _) => {
502                self.blend_buf.push([T::Numeric::ZERO; SCRATCH_BUF_SIZE]);
503            }
504            Cmd::PopBuf => {
505                self.blend_buf.pop();
506            }
507            Cmd::ClipFill(cf) => {
508                self.clip(cf.x as usize, cf.width as usize, None);
509            }
510            Cmd::ClipStrip(cs) => {
511                let clip_attrs = &attrs.clip[cs.attrs_idx as usize];
512                let alpha_idx = clip_attrs.alpha_idx(cs.alpha_offset) as usize;
513                self.clip(cs.x as usize, cs.width as usize, Some(&alphas[alpha_idx..]));
514            }
515            Cmd::Blend(b) => self.blend(*b),
516            Cmd::Mask(m) => {
517                let start_x = self.wide_coords.0 * WideTile::WIDTH;
518                let start_y = self.wide_coords.1 * Tile::HEIGHT;
519
520                let blend_buf = self.blend_buf.last_mut().unwrap();
521
522                let width = (blend_buf.len() / (Tile::HEIGHT as usize * COLOR_COMPONENTS)) as u16;
523                let y = start_y as u32 + u32x4::from_slice(self.simd, &[0, 1, 2, 3]);
524
525                let iter = (start_x..(start_x + width)).map(|x| {
526                    let x_in_range = x < m.width();
527
528                    macro_rules! sample {
529                        ($idx:expr) => {
530                            if x_in_range && (y[$idx] as u16) < m.height() { m.sample(x, y[$idx] as u16) } else { 0 }
531                        };
532                    }
533
534                    let s1 = sample!(0);
535                    let s2 = sample!(1);
536                    let s3 = sample!(2);
537                    let s4 = sample!(3);
538
539                    let samples = u8x16::from_slice(self.simd, &[s1, s1, s1, s1, s2, s2, s2, s2, s3, s3, s3, s3, s4, s4, s4, s4]);
540                    T::NumericVec::from_u8(self.simd, samples)
541                });
542
543                T::apply_mask(self.simd, blend_buf, iter);
544            }
545            Cmd::Opacity(o) => {
546                if *o != 1.0 {
547                    let blend_buf = self.blend_buf.last_mut().unwrap();
548
549                    T::apply_mask(self.simd, blend_buf, iter::repeat(T::NumericVec::from_f32(self.simd, f32x16::splat(self.simd, *o))));
550                }
551            }
552            Cmd::PushZeroClip(_) | Cmd::PopZeroClip => {
553                // These commands are handled by the dispatcher and should not reach fine rasterization
554                unreachable!();
555            }
556            Cmd::BatchEnd => {}
557        }
558    }
559
560    /// Fill a horizontal strip within the current tile using the given paint.
561    ///
562    /// This is the core painting method that handles solid colors, gradients, images,
563    /// and blurred rounded rectangles. It applies the paint starting at the given x
564    /// coordinate with the specified width, using the provided blend mode.
565    ///
566    /// Note: For short strip segments, benchmarks showed that not inlining this method
567    /// leads to significantly worse performance.
568    pub fn fill(
569        &mut self,
570        x: usize,
571        width: usize,
572        fill: &Paint,
573        blend_mode: BlendMode,
574        encoded_paints: &[EncodedPaint],
575        image_resolver: &dyn ImageResolver,
576        alphas: Option<&[u8]>,
577        mask: Option<&Mask>,
578    ) {
579        let blend_buf = &mut self.blend_buf.last_mut().unwrap()[x * TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS..][..TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS * width];
580        let default_blend = blend_mode == BlendMode::default();
581
582        match fill {
583            Paint::Solid(color) => {
584                let color = T::extract_color(*color);
585
586                // If color is completely opaque, we can just directly override
587                // the blend buffer.
588                if color[3] == T::Numeric::ONE && default_blend && alphas.is_none() && mask.is_none() {
589                    T::copy_solid(self.simd, blend_buf, color);
590
591                    return;
592                }
593
594                if default_blend && mask.is_none() {
595                    T::alpha_composite_solid(self.simd, blend_buf, color, alphas);
596                } else {
597                    let start_x = self.wide_coords.0 * WideTile::WIDTH + x as u16;
598                    let start_y = self.wide_coords.1 * Tile::HEIGHT;
599
600                    T::blend(
601                        self.simd,
602                        blend_buf,
603                        start_x,
604                        start_y,
605                        iter::repeat(T::Composite::from_color(self.simd, color)),
606                        blend_mode,
607                        alphas,
608                        mask,
609                    );
610                }
611            }
612            Paint::Indexed(paint) => {
613                let color_buf = &mut self.paint_buf[x * TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS..][..TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS * width];
614
615                let encoded_paint = &encoded_paints[paint.index()];
616
617                let start_x = self.wide_coords.0 * WideTile::WIDTH + x as u16;
618                let start_y = self.wide_coords.1 * Tile::HEIGHT;
619
620                // Make sure sampling happens at the center of the pixel.
621                let sampler_x = start_x as f64 + PIXEL_CENTER_OFFSET;
622                let sampler_y = start_y as f64 + PIXEL_CENTER_OFFSET;
623
624                // We need to have this as a macro because closures cannot take generic arguments, and
625                // we would have to repeatedly provide all arguments if we made it a function.
626                macro_rules! fill_complex_paint {
627                    ($may_have_transparency:expr, $filler:expr) => {
628                        fill_complex_paint!($may_have_transparency, $filler, None::<&Tint>)
629                    };
630                    ($may_have_transparency:expr, $filler:expr, $tint:expr) => {
631                        if $may_have_transparency || alphas.is_some() {
632                            T::apply_painter(self.simd, color_buf, $filler);
633                            if let Some(t) = $tint {
634                                T::apply_tint(self.simd, color_buf, t);
635                            }
636
637                            if default_blend && mask.is_none() {
638                                T::alpha_composite_buffer(self.simd, blend_buf, color_buf, alphas);
639                            } else {
640                                T::blend(
641                                    self.simd,
642                                    blend_buf,
643                                    start_x,
644                                    start_y,
645                                    color_buf.chunks_exact(T::Composite::LENGTH).map(|s| T::Composite::from_slice(self.simd, s)),
646                                    blend_mode,
647                                    alphas,
648                                    mask,
649                                );
650                            }
651                        } else {
652                            // Similarly to solid colors we can just override the previous values
653                            // if all colors in the gradient are fully opaque.
654                            T::apply_painter(self.simd, blend_buf, $filler);
655                            if let Some(t) = $tint {
656                                T::apply_tint(self.simd, blend_buf, t);
657                            }
658                        }
659                    };
660                }
661
662                match encoded_paint {
663                    EncodedPaint::BlurredRoundedRect(b) => {
664                        fill_complex_paint!(true, T::blurred_rounded_rectangle_painter(self.simd, b, sampler_x, sampler_y));
665                    }
666                    EncodedPaint::Gradient(g) => {
667                        // Note that we are calculating the t values first, store them in a separate
668                        // buffer and then pass that buffer to the iterator instead of calculating
669                        // the t values on the fly in the iterator. The latter would be faster, but
670                        // it would probably increase code size a lot, because the functions for
671                        // position calculation need to be inlined for good performance.
672                        let f32_buf = &mut self.f32_buf[..width * Tile::HEIGHT as usize];
673
674                        match &g.kind {
675                            EncodedKind::Linear(l) => {
676                                calculate_t_vals(self.simd, SimdLinearKind::new(self.simd, *l), f32_buf, g, sampler_x, sampler_y);
677
678                                fill_complex_paint!(g.may_have_transparency, T::gradient_painter(self.simd, g, f32_buf));
679                            }
680                            EncodedKind::Sweep(s) => {
681                                calculate_t_vals(self.simd, SimdSweepKind::new(self.simd, s), f32_buf, g, sampler_x, sampler_y);
682
683                                fill_complex_paint!(g.may_have_transparency, T::gradient_painter(self.simd, g, f32_buf));
684                            }
685                            EncodedKind::Radial(r) => {
686                                calculate_t_vals(self.simd, SimdRadialKind::new(self.simd, r), f32_buf, g, sampler_x, sampler_y);
687
688                                if r.has_undefined() {
689                                    fill_complex_paint!(g.may_have_transparency, T::gradient_painter_with_undefined(self.simd, g, f32_buf));
690                                } else {
691                                    fill_complex_paint!(g.may_have_transparency, T::gradient_painter(self.simd, g, f32_buf));
692                                }
693                            }
694                        }
695                    }
696                    EncodedPaint::Image(i) => {
697                        let pixmap = match &i.source {
698                            ImageSource::Pixmap(p) => p.clone(),
699                            ImageSource::OpaqueId { id, .. } => {
700                                image_resolver.resolve(*id).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("Image {:?} not found in registry", id))
701                            }
702                        };
703
704                        let tint = i.tint.as_ref();
705
706                        match (i.has_skew(), i.nearest_neighbor()) {
707                            (false, false) => {
708                                // Axis-aligned with filtering - use optimized plain painters
709                                if i.sampler.quality == ImageQuality::Medium {
710                                    fill_complex_paint!(
711                                        i.may_have_transparency,
712                                        T::plain_medium_quality_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y),
713                                        tint
714                                    );
715                                } else {
716                                    fill_complex_paint!(
717                                        i.may_have_transparency,
718                                        T::high_quality_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y),
719                                        tint
720                                    );
721                                }
722                            }
723                            (true, false) => {
724                                // Skewed with filtering - use generic filtered painters
725                                if i.sampler.quality == ImageQuality::Medium {
726                                    fill_complex_paint!(
727                                        i.may_have_transparency,
728                                        T::medium_quality_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y),
729                                        tint
730                                    );
731                                } else {
732                                    fill_complex_paint!(
733                                        i.may_have_transparency,
734                                        T::high_quality_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y),
735                                        tint
736                                    );
737                                }
738                            }
739                            (false, true) => {
740                                fill_complex_paint!(
741                                    i.may_have_transparency,
742                                    T::plain_nn_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y),
743                                    tint
744                                );
745                            }
746                            (true, true) => {
747                                fill_complex_paint!(i.may_have_transparency, T::nn_image_painter(self.simd, i, &pixmap, sampler_x, sampler_y), tint);
748                            }
749                        }
750                    }
751                    EncodedPaint::ExternalTexture(_) => {
752                        unimplemented!("External textures are not supported by `vello_cpu`")
753                    }
754                }
755            }
756        }
757    }
758
759    /// Blend the top blend buffer into the buffer below it.
760    ///
761    /// This pops the top buffer from the blend stack and composites it onto the
762    /// buffer below using the specified blend mode. This is the core operation for
763    /// layer composition.
764    pub(crate) fn blend(&mut self, blend_mode: BlendMode) {
765        let (source_buffer, rest) = self.blend_buf.split_last_mut().unwrap();
766        let target_buffer = rest.last_mut().unwrap();
767
768        if blend_mode == BlendMode::default() {
769            T::alpha_composite_buffer(self.simd, target_buffer, source_buffer, None);
770        } else {
771            T::blend(
772                self.simd,
773                target_buffer,
774                // `start_x` and `start_y` are only needed to sample the correct position
775                // of a mask, so we can just pass dummy values here.
776                0,
777                0,
778                source_buffer.chunks_exact(T::Composite::LENGTH).map(|s| T::Composite::from_slice(self.simd, s)),
779                blend_mode,
780                None,
781                None,
782            );
783        }
784    }
785
786    /// Apply a clipping mask from the top buffer to the buffer below.
787    ///
788    /// Uses the top buffer's alpha channel as a mask, multiplying it with the buffer
789    /// below. This implements clipping by masking out pixels outside the clip region.
790    fn clip(&mut self, x: usize, width: usize, alphas: Option<&[u8]>) {
791        let (source_buffer, rest) = self.blend_buf.split_last_mut().unwrap();
792        let target_buffer = rest.last_mut().unwrap();
793
794        let source_buffer = &mut source_buffer[x * TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS..][..TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS * width];
795        let target_buffer = &mut target_buffer[x * TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS..][..TILE_HEIGHT_COMPONENTS * width];
796
797        T::alpha_composite_buffer(self.simd, target_buffer, source_buffer, alphas);
798    }
799}
800
801/// A trait for objects that can render pixel data into buffers.
802///
803/// Painters abstract over different content sources (gradients, images, etc.) and can
804/// generate pixel data in either u8 or f32 format. Implementations should provide at least
805/// one of these methods; the other can delegate through conversion.
806///
807/// Note: Some painters may only efficiently support one numeric type. The implementation
808/// may convert between types as needed.
809pub trait Painter {
810    /// Paint pixel data into a u8 buffer (values in 0-255 range).
811    fn paint_u8(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]);
812
813    /// Paint pixel data into an f32 buffer (values in 0.0-1.0 range).
814    fn paint_f32(&mut self, buf: &mut [f32]);
815}
816
817/// Extension trait for creating position vectors for gradient and image sampling.
818///
819/// This trait provides a method to generate SIMD vectors of positions that advance
820/// correctly across a tile. It's used by painters to compute per-pixel coordinates
821/// for sampling operations.
822pub trait PosExt<S: Simd> {
823    /// Create a position vector that advances appropriately across a tile.
824    ///
825    /// Given a starting position and per-pixel advances in x and y directions,
826    /// generates a SIMD vector with the correct position for each element.
827    fn splat_pos(simd: S, pos: f32, x_advance: f32, y_advance: f32) -> Self;
828}
829
830impl<S: Simd> PosExt<S> for f32x4<S> {
831    #[inline(always)]
832    fn splat_pos(simd: S, pos: f32, _: f32, y_advance: f32) -> Self {
833        let columns: [f32; Tile::HEIGHT as usize] = [0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0];
834        let column_mask: Self = columns.simd_into(simd);
835
836        column_mask.mul_add(Self::splat(simd, y_advance), Self::splat(simd, pos))
837    }
838}
839
840impl<S: Simd> PosExt<S> for f32x8<S> {
841    #[inline(always)]
842    fn splat_pos(simd: S, pos: f32, x_advance: f32, y_advance: f32) -> Self {
843        simd.combine_f32x4(f32x4::splat_pos(simd, pos, x_advance, y_advance), f32x4::splat_pos(simd, pos + x_advance, x_advance, y_advance))
844    }
845}
846
847/// Intermediate shader result with color channels stored separately for efficient processing.
848///
849/// This structure holds 8 pixels worth of data in planar format (separate R, G, B, A vectors).
850/// The planar layout is more efficient for certain SIMD operations before final interleaving.
851pub(crate) struct ShaderResultF32<S: Simd> {
852    /// Red channel values for 8 pixels.
853    pub(crate) r: f32x8<S>,
854    /// Green channel values for 8 pixels.
855    pub(crate) g: f32x8<S>,
856    /// Blue channel values for 8 pixels.
857    pub(crate) b: f32x8<S>,
858    /// Alpha channel values for 8 pixels.
859    pub(crate) a: f32x8<S>,
860}
861
862impl<S: Simd> ShaderResultF32<S> {
863    /// Convert from planar format to interleaved RGBA format.
864    ///
865    /// Returns two f32x16 vectors containing 8 pixels (4 RGBA components each)
866    /// with channels interleaved in the standard RGBA order.
867    #[inline(always)]
868    pub(crate) fn get(&self) -> (f32x16<S>, f32x16<S>) {
869        let (r_1, r_2) = self.r.simd.split_f32x8(self.r);
870        let (g_1, g_2) = self.g.simd.split_f32x8(self.g);
871        let (b_1, b_2) = self.b.simd.split_f32x8(self.b);
872        let (a_1, a_2) = self.a.simd.split_f32x8(self.a);
873
874        let first = self.r.simd.combine_f32x8(self.r.simd.combine_f32x4(r_1, g_1), self.r.simd.combine_f32x4(b_1, a_1));
875
876        let second = self.r.simd.combine_f32x8(self.r.simd.combine_f32x4(r_2, g_2), self.r.simd.combine_f32x4(b_2, a_2));
877
878        (first, second)
879    }
880}
881
882mod macros {
883    /// Implements the `Painter` trait for an iterator that produces f32x16 SIMD vectors.
884    ///
885    /// This macro generates both `paint_u8` and `paint_f32` methods, converting between
886    /// formats as needed. Used for painters that work natively with high-precision f32 data.
887    macro_rules! f32x16_painter {
888        ($($type_path:tt)+) => {
889            impl<S: Simd> crate::third_party::vello_cpu::fine::Painter for $($type_path)+ {
890                fn paint_u8(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) {
891                    use crate::third_party::vello_common::fearless_simd::*;
892                    use crate::third_party::vello_cpu::fine::NumericVec;
893
894                    self.simd.vectorize(#[inline(always)] || {
895                        for chunk in buf.chunks_exact_mut(16) {
896                            let next = self.next().unwrap();
897                            let converted = u8x16::<S>::from_f32(next.simd, next);
898                            converted.store_slice(chunk);
899                        }
900                    })
901                }
902
903                fn paint_f32(&mut self, buf: &mut [f32]) {
904                    self.simd.vectorize(#[inline(always)] || {
905                        for chunk in buf.chunks_exact_mut(16) {
906                            let next = self.next().unwrap();
907                            next.store_slice(chunk);
908                        }
909                    })
910                }
911            }
912        };
913    }
914
915    /// Implements the `Painter` trait for an iterator that produces u8x16 SIMD vectors.
916    ///
917    /// This macro generates both `paint_u8` and `paint_f32` methods, converting between
918    /// formats as needed. Used for painters that work natively with low-precision u8 data.
919    macro_rules! u8x16_painter {
920        ($($type_path:tt)+) => {
921            impl<S: Simd> crate::third_party::vello_cpu::fine::Painter for $($type_path)+ {
922                fn paint_u8(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) {
923                    self.simd.vectorize(#[inline(always)] || {
924                        for chunk in buf.chunks_exact_mut(16) {
925                            let next = self.next().unwrap();
926                            next.store_slice(chunk);
927                        }
928                    })
929                }
930
931                fn paint_f32(&mut self, buf: &mut [f32]) {
932                    use crate::third_party::vello_common::fearless_simd::*;
933                    use crate::third_party::vello_cpu::fine::NumericVec;
934
935                    self.simd.vectorize(#[inline(always)] || {
936                        for chunk in buf.chunks_exact_mut(16) {
937                            let next = self.next().unwrap();
938                            let converted = f32x16::<S>::from_u8(next.simd, next);
939                            converted.store_slice(chunk);
940                        }
941                    })
942                }
943            }
944        };
945    }
946
947    pub(crate) use f32x16_painter;
948    pub(crate) use u8x16_painter;
949}
